steps.what: Check medical and pharmaceutical supplies and capture actual quantities, use and storage observations
Compile supply use totals and compare recorded quantities and expiry dates with selected thresholds
Monitor supply status by investigating discrepancies and deciding appropriate escalation or replenishment requests

tasks.design: Configure a native stock view in {OTHER}, the clinical supply inventory system, replacing repeated totals in {SPREADSHEET}. The nurse retains physical checks, observation capture, discrepancy investigation and decisions about supply follow-up; no medication choice or dispensing action is automated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated compilation of supply movements and date comparisons distracted from checking actual stock concerns.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit quantities, units and recorded dates can be compared through native inventory views.
tasks.still_hard: A sufficient recorded count does not establish suitable condition, correct storage or availability for actual care.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse recognises when recorded supply status conflicts with what care delivery requires.
tasks.altitude: Less supply arithmetic; monitoring responsibility and existing clinical authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Reconcile supply quantities and storage concerns
reach.learn: Stock units, provenance and appropriate escalation

evidence.claim: Native stock views can compare explicit counts and expiry dates without establishing clinical suitability; the proposed hours are unmeasured model scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is monitoring supply use and status, excluding prescribing, dispensing, purchasing approval and administering care. Assign each physical count and movement record once across roles.

Normal receiving and issue staff produce supply movement records through unchanged work. Nurse counts, checks and captures item identifier, batch, location, quantity and unit, observed condition, recorded expiry date, observation time and source movement reference in s1's 35 hours; no free structured stock or safe-to-use flag is assumed.

Supply or pharmacy owners maintain existing stock requirements. Nurse selects and records the applicable version, explicit quantity threshold and expiry warning interval within s1; no new par level is assumed. Additional rule-field upkeep is counted below.

s2 performs arithmetic and date comparison only. Missing batches, incompatible units or uncertain dates remain unknown and return to manual checking and investigation in s3's retained 50 hours. No automatic substitution, disposal, order or clinical recommendation is proposed.
Try native inventory configuration first. Applicable local supply and professional requirements need customer confirmation; existing pharmacy decisions and work remain outside the focal denominator.
unknowns: Whether native inventory records match actual supply units and locations
Which supply monitoring rules the nurse is authorized to use
research_questions: Does the native view reproduce known supply discrepancies without treating incomplete records as suitable stock?

already_counted.description: Capture actual supply observations, select monitoring rules and investigate concerns and exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain inventory mappings and retest threshold views

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85, gross=15; subtract 7 focal upkeep for central net=8. Range assumes incomplete stock records and manual batch investigation. Two other-role upkeep hours are recorded separately; physical checks and suitability judgement keep full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct or provide home health services

steps.what: Assess the home care situation and direct appropriate health services within professional authority
Provide home health services and respond to the patient's actual needs and circumstances

tasks.design: Keep home care direction and delivery human, using the current plan in {OTHER}, the clinical record system. The nurse assesses the real home context and provides care within the existing professional and organizational arrangements.
tasks.previous_blocker: Home care depends on direct assessment, patient participation and changing circumstances.
tasks.enabler_now: Current native care records already support the work; no new automated care decision is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Needs and circumstances may change during a visit and require professional judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse develops trust and notices concerns that may not appear in the written plan.
tasks.altitude: Home care effort and existing professional decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate home care around actual patient needs
reach.learn: Continuity of care and contextual observation

evidence.claim: Directing and providing home health services require professional human assessment and care; documentation capabilities do not demonstrate a saving in care delivery.

assumptions: Boundary is human home care assessment, direction and delivery, excluding scheduling, travel administration and separately owned note drafting. No clinical paperwork baseline is invented inside direct care.

Existing care teams produce the current plan through unchanged care work. Patient and nurse produce the observed home context during s1; patient responses and care observations continue during s2. Nurse elicits, interprets and captures relevant information within the retained 100 hours, without a free structured care-need flag.

Existing scope of practice and escalation arrangements remain in place and need local confirmation. Keep native care records with no new recording, model or care workflow, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Local professional scope and home care responsibilities
How care continuity and escalation are arranged
research_questions: Do home care direction and actual delivery reflect the patient's current needs and agreed care plan?

already_counted.description: Assess home circumstances, direct services and provide human care

incremental.description: No changed care process or new upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Assessment and care delivery keep full effort; no patient or other clinician time is claimed as a focal saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Teach classes in mental health topics and adapt explanations to participants' understanding and questions

tasks.design: Keep mental health teaching human, using current vetted teaching materials in {DOCS}. The nurse explains, listens and adapts to participant understanding while separating general instruction from questions needing individual follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Teaching depends on participant understanding and sensitive questions rather than simply presenting text.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing native teaching materials already support classes; no new automated advice is required.
tasks.still_hard: Participants may interpret general information through personal experiences that need careful clarification.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse builds trust and recognises when a question needs private or individualized attention.
tasks.altitude: Teaching time and professional responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Support understanding of mental health care information

evidence.claim: Mental health teaching requires responsive human explanation and observation of understanding; no saving is claimed for replacing that interaction with generated text.

assumptions: Boundary is conducting classes, excluding enrolment, scheduling, developing general teaching resources and individual clinical consultations. Shared teaching and care interactions must have one owner.

Existing educators or clinicians provide vetted materials through normal preparation. Participants produce questions and responses during the class before the corresponding clarification; nurse elicits, checks and captures understanding within the retained 100 hours. No free structured comprehension or emotional-state flag is assumed.
Keep native materials and current teaching practice. No participant profiling, recording or model advice is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Class format and participants' learning needs
How questions needing individual attention are followed up
research_questions: Can participants explain the intended general concepts and identify where individual follow-up is appropriate?

already_counted.description: Explain mental health topics, listen to questions and adapt instruction

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Class explanation and responsive discussion retain full effort; no preparation or individual care saving is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: A small reduction in supply arithmetic is possible, while home care and mental health teaching retain full human responsibility and time.
reach: Review supply provenance with pharmacy technicians
Coordinate contextual home care with registered nurses
Discuss clear mental health explanations with psychiatric technicians
skills_to_grow: Separate recorded supply status from actual condition
Capture inventory rules and observations explicitly
Teach and provide care responsively in context
role.ambitious_version: Maintain dependable supply oversight while protecting the professional presence and judgement needed for care and education.
